audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 1-3 were all marked Skill while the whys say Ziggs pokes for free at 1, 'wins every level-2 skirmish where you commit your hook', and still holds a range advantage at 3 that forces Sylas to outplay him just to trade evenly. The first-item row was marked Sylas while whys[5] describes Ziggs nearly one-shotting you on the approach. Packet chart reads Ziggs, Ziggs, Ziggs, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill.
audit.why: Ziggs's 850-range Q against a champion whose longest tool is 775 means the early rows genuinely belong to him. Level 6 is Sylas's, and the item rows are close.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-2 set to Ziggs and row 5 to Skill in both layers; ratings rescaled.

audit.why: Four spikes covering levels 1-3, level 6, levels 4-5 and Ziggs's first item. Timings are right; spikes[1]'s content was wrong (point 4) and is corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four issues. (a) The page says three times that Hijacking Mega Inferno Bomb makes Ziggs 'lose his primary long-range threat' / 'lose his primary engage tool' / have 'no R to defend'. Sylas's R copies an ultimate and casts it freely — it does not remove the owner's. (b) The mid text says a landed pull leaves him 'stunned in your face'; Sylas's E has no CC. (c) Bouncing Bomb's range is given as 900; it is 850 (900 is Hexplosive Minefield). (d) Short Fuse's auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: The stolen-ult error is the worst of the three: a player will dive at 6 believing Ziggs has been disarmed and take a Mega Inferno Bomb to the face on the way in. The stun claim similarly promises lockdown that does not exist.
audit.corrected: All three 'he loses his R' claims replaced with the truth that Hijack copies rather than takes, keyed to his real 120-second cooldown; the stun claim replaced with the actual requirement to follow up instantly; Q corrected to 850; Short Fuse named as an auto-reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is named the matchup-defining cooldown in six places without its length ever appearing, and whys[3] calls it 'a long cooldown' in the abstract.
audit.why: 20 seconds at rank 1 down to 12 at rank 5 is the entire scheduling problem of this lane — the advice 'commit on its cooldown' is unusable without it.
audit.corrected: 20-second rank-1 figure written into early, whys[1], report[5].t and dosFull[0].d.

audit.why: Packet flagged wants.you[2] 'Steal Mega Inferno Bomb' as a suspect name; it is his real R. False positive, left alone.

edits.before: His W knockback interrupts your E chain pull the moment the projectile appears — he holds it reactively and wins every level-2 skirmish where you commit your hook.
edits.after: Satchel Charge knocks you away the moment your chain is in the air, and he holds it reactively — at 20 seconds rank 1 he still wins every level-2 skirmish you start.

edits.before: Stealing Mega Inferno Bomb gives you his best teamfight and siege tool with your AP scaling — he loses his primary long-range threat and cannot safely pressure you off the wave.
edits.after: Stealing Mega Inferno Bomb gives you his siege and teamfight tool on your own AP — Hijack copies it rather than taking it, but at 120 seconds his is the slower clock.

edits.before: Stealing Mega Inferno Bomb flips the script: you get a global nuke with your AP scaling and he loses his primary engage/teamfight tool.
edits.after: Stealing Mega Inferno Bomb flips the script: a 5000-range nuke on your own AP — Hijack copies his R, it does not disarm him.

edits.before: At level 1 you have Q or W and no reliable way to close the 900-range gap on Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb — accept the poke, farm with Q at maximum range, and do not walk past the wave into his bombs. Level 2 changes nothing because his W knockback can interrupt your E pull the instant your chain is in the air; hold your E until you see him place Satchel Charge or it goes on cooldown. Level 3 is your first real window: if he wastes W on the wave or misses a placement, dash in with E-first-tap, fire the chain hook past his minefield hitbox, and chain into W-Kingslayer before he can reposition. Even then he will likely burn flash — take the trade, it is a win.
edits.after: At level 1 you have Q or W and no reliable way to close the 850 range of Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb — accept the poke, farm with Q at maximum range, and do not walk past the wave into his bombs. Level 2 changes nothing, because Satchel Charge knocks you away the instant your chain is in the air; hold your E until you see him place it or it goes on cooldown, and at rank 1 that is a 20-second wait. Level 3 is your first real window: if he spends it on the wave or misplaces it, dash in with E-first-tap, fire the chain past his minefield hitbox, and chain into W-Kingslayer before he can reposition. Even then he will likely burn flash — take the trade, it is a win.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 shift the equation as your E cooldown shortens and you learn his repositioning habits. He will almost always pre-place E (minefield) in the expected hook path — train him by faking dashes at minion clusters, then fire the real hook from an angle where the minefield does not overlap. If you hit the pull, he is stunned in your face with no escapes; your Passive chain autos plus W at his missing-health threshold burst him in one rotation. Level 6 is your defining moment: steal Mega Inferno Bomb, use it immediately on him or toward his tower, and convert the pressure into a dive or a forced recall. He has no R to defend and you now have a global threat he respects for the rest of the game.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 shift the equation as your E cooldown shortens and you learn his repositioning habits. He will almost always pre-place Hexplosive Minefield in the expected hook path — train him by faking dashes at minion clusters, then fire the real hook from an angle the minefield does not cover. If you hit the pull you are on top of him with no CC of your own, so the follow-up has to be instant: passive chain autos plus W-Kingslayer burst him in one rotation. Level 6 is your defining moment: steal Mega Inferno Bomb and use it immediately on him or toward his tower. Hijack copies his R rather than taking it, but his own is 120 seconds at rank 1, so your copy is genuinely extra pressure.

edits.before: Track Ziggs’s Satchel Charge: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Satchel Charge, 20s at rank 1 — he is catchable only while it is down. Short Fuse is an auto-reset; read the wind-up.

edits.before: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: His knockback escape, 20 seconds at rank 1 — he is catchable only while it is down. Never commit into it.

notes: The page claimed three separate times that stealing Mega Inferno Bomb strips Ziggs of his ultimate — it does not; Sylas copies it. That is the kind of error that gets a player killed diving at 6. Two data inconsistencies I did not touch: the full layer sets diff to 'FAV' while breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both read 'Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10', and the kit file carries a percentHealth flag on Satchel Charge that Riot's own description does not support (it says only 'deals magic damage'), so I did not write percent-health damage into the page. Both are in questionsForUser / unverified.
